{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM Services Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of IBM Base Terms — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Base Terms against our playbook and verified 19 findings. Seven positions are already acceptable and require no redline: IBM's IP indemnity (§ 8.1) sits at our fallback and is in fact better than fallback on the cap (indemnity payments are carved out of the $100,000 / twelve-month cap by § 9.1(a)), and we carry no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation burden (§ 14.16 Freedom of Action is helpful to us here).

The substantive work sits in three clusters:

- **Two critical/high IP and licence gaps.** Type II Materials default to IBM ownership with a licence back that is neither perpetual, royalty-free, modifiable, sublicensable nor scoped to our business, and § 14.18 lets IBM exploit our contact information for its own marketing and disclose it onward (§ 5.4 / § 7 / § 14.18). Separately, the Base Components licence runs to Bluefly, Inc. alone with no Affiliate coverage (§ 12.1).
- **Two walk-away items.** IBM has **no insurance obligation of any kind** despite hosting our environment and processing personal data, and IBM's investigation right in § 11.3 is unlimited in frequency, requires no notice and allocates no cost.
- **A cluster of exit, remedy and liability shortfalls.** No transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (§ 3.5); no warranty period or remedy, with all Materials "AS IS" (§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c)); convenience termination limited to calendar month-end with no refund of prepaid charges and uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4); no carve-outs from the mutual liability caps for confidentiality, gross negligence or willful misconduct, made worse by § 6's precedence over the confidentiality agreement; one-way assignment favouring IBM (§ 14.10); and New York law with no forum specified at all (§ 14.3).

One finding (**RENEWAL, § 3.2**) failed verification and is marked needs review before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (fallback) | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | Uncapped IP indemnity via § 9.1(a) carve-out; no redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with § 7, § 14.18) | Type II licence back not perpetual/royalty-free/modifiable/sublicensable; IBM markets our contact data. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No sourcing restriction on us. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Grant runs to Bluefly, Inc. only; no Affiliate mechanism. |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No field-of-use or competing-product restriction. |
| 6 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | One-way: IBM may assign freely, including to a competitor. |
| 7 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unlimited frequency, no notice, no cost allocation. |
| 8 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14.3 Choice of Law | NY law is preferred, but no forum specified anywhere. |
| 9 | Medium | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Early termination charges set outside the Agreement and uncapped. |
| 10 | Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | No confidentiality / gross negligence / willful misconduct carve-outs; § 6 caps confidentiality breach. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No MFN burden on us. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant (preferred) | § 4.1 Charges | Charges tied to Services ordered; confirm Order Forms/SOAs. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant (preferred) | § 14.8 Personnel | No no-hire covenant. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal notice window | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 3.2 Renewal | 90-day non-renewal window exceeds our 60-day ceiling; re-verify before sending. |
| 15 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Month-end anchor only; no refund of prepaid charges. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition, return, export or deletion obligation. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | No conformance warranty, no period, no remedy; § 5.4(c) "AS IS". |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | No insurance obligation for a hosting provider handling personal data. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These two must be resolved; we should not sign as drafted.

1. **Vendor insurance — absent entirely (§ 14.12 / miscellaneous).** IBM hosts our environment and, per § 14.18, processes personal information on our behalf, yet carries no contractual coverage obligation. We are inserting a short clause at the preferred level: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M where IBM handles data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request. Fallback available: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
2. **Unbounded investigation right (§ 11.3).** IBM may investigate suspected AUP violations with no frequency limit, no advance notice (the notice paragraph applies only before IBM restricts access or removes Content, and is excused in an emergency) and no cost allocation. We propose the fallback cure only: one investigation per year, 15 days' notice, IBM bears cost unless an underpayment exceeding 10% is found.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify RENEWAL (§ 3.2)** before comments go out — the finding failed verification. Substantively we expect to substitute sixty (60) days for ninety (90) days, retaining the mutual notice right, writing requirement, per-Attachment structure and term-end anchor. Renewal carries no uplift, so the price-cap point is not engaged; if any Service Option Attachment term exceeds 12 months we escalate to cap the renewal term at 12 months.
2. **Issue the redline** covering the deviations and gaps above, each at the level noted: IP (licence attributes plus business-purpose scope; confine IBM's use of our contact information to providing the Services); LICENSE (extend § 12.1 to Affiliates on written notice); ASSIGN (mutual successor right on notice, other assignments on consent not unreasonably withheld); GOVLAW (add exclusive New York County forum, leaving the choice-of-law sentence verbatim); LD (cap early termination charges at three months' charges and make them our sole liquidated amount); LOL-CAP (one mutual carve-out sentence in §§ 9.1(c) and 9.2(c)); T4C (express convenience right, 30 days' notice, remove the month-end anchor, pro-rata refund of prepaid charges); TRANSITION (insert transition assistance, Content return and certified deletion into § 3.5, which survives under § 14.2); WARRANTY (90-day software conformance, 30-day Services warranty, repair/replace/re-perform and refund, plus a carve-out from the § 5.4(c) AS IS disclaimer).
3. **Diligence on documents not before us:** confirm Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms contain no minimum volumes, minimum monthly charges or early termination amounts inconsistent with the LD and MINCOMMIT positions, and confirm no Attachment term exceeds 12 months.
4. **Note for the business, not redlined:** the broad Type I Materials licence back to IBM; the absence of an IBM-granted MFN in our favour; and, under INDEMN, the twelve-month refund-credit cap, the strict prompt-notice condition, and the breadth of our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity for Services Recipient claims (partly mitigated by the § 8.2(c) carve-back for IBM's fault). We can raise any of these commercially if the negotiation allows."}
